hints: Look closely at Q in the photomicrograph. Notice its very wide, empty lumen, thick wall, and its position in neat rows inside the vascular bundle.
Remember the difference between dead water-conducting cells and living cells. Which type has lignin and pits but no cytoplasm for plasmodesmata?
walkthrough:
**Identify cell Q**

Look at where Q is pointing. It is one of the large, open, white circles in the xylem of the vascular bundle.

These are xylem vessel elements. They are wide, hollow tubes with thick walls, specialised for transporting water up the stem.

**Check statements 1 and 2**

Xylem vessel walls are strengthened with both cellulose and lignin. This gives support and waterproofing.

They also have pits, which are thin areas or gaps in the lignified wall where water can move sideways between vessels.

**Check statement 3 and conclude**

Plasmodesmata are living cytoplasmic links between living cells.

Mature xylem vessels are dead with no cytoplasm, so they cannot have plasmodesmata. Statement 3 is false.

So only 1 and 2 are correct, which is option A.

options.A: Correct. Q is a xylem vessel, which has pits (1) and a wall of cellulose plus lignin (2), but no plasmodesmata.
options.B: Incorrect. Although 1 is true, 3 is false because mature xylem vessels are dead and have no living plasmodesmata connections.
options.C: Incorrect. Statement 1 alone is incomplete because statement 2 is also true for the lignified wall of xylem.
options.D: Incorrect. Although 2 is true, 3 is false for the same reason, dead xylem vessels cannot be linked by living plasmodesmata.
